result.summary:
The Steam Deck check at 1280x800 is done. On the Deck the game shows at 1:1 scale with nothing stretched or cut off, and it can be played with the built-in controller alone. Screenshots of every menu screen and the race HUD (day, night, rain, countdown, tutorial hint, refuelling, police chase, City Limits and towing, finish, pause) were rendered under Xvfb before and after the changes. I checked the scaling inside the running game: the window is 1280x800, the content is 1280x720 at scale 1.0 shifted 40 px down, so there are 40 px black bars top and bottom.

What was wrong before:
- **Text below 9 px x-height:** the HUD police distance (16 px, 8 px x-height), "CITY LIMITS" (13 px capitals, 9 px), the stage-screen info tiles (16 px; "Abenddämmerung" also ran 5 px past its tile), the "Nächste Etappe …" line on the route cards (16 px), and the version number on the title screen (16 px). The HUD texts at 17 px were right at the 9 px limit. Godot renders text the same way as FreeType, which I confirmed by measuring screenshots.
- **Contrast:** the km labels under the HUD progress bar stood directly on the sky, giving 1.5:1 to 3:1 in daylight. The dimmed capital labels in the menus (table headers, tile captions) were at 3.4 to 3.9:1.
- **Gamepad:** the player name field in Options could only be filled with a keyboard. Every footer showed keyboard keycaps next to the pad buttons. The tutorial opened with two keyboard tips, and the gamepad tip only came about 14 seconds after the start.

What I changed:
- **Gamepad-only hints:** a new `InputMode` tracks the active device. With a pad, footers show only pad glyphs (A/B/X/Y, LT/RT, a drawn D-pad instead of arrow keys, an LS stick glyph). A key press switches back to the old mixed display; mouse, touch and trackpads don't switch.
- **Tutorial:** with a pad, it shows only the gamepad tip.
- **Options name field:** pad A opens the existing on-screen keyboard (new `NameEntryBox`).
- **HUD:** stage name, record line, km labels and "frei" go from 17 to 19 px, "km/h" to 18, police distance to 18, "CITY LIMITS" to 15. The km labels now sit on the progress-bar panel (daytime contrast 12.2:1 and 6.2:1 instead of 3.0:1 and 1.5:1). The penalty badge sits in that row. HUD panels are slightly darker (opacity 0.62 to 0.72). Names that are too long are cut with "…".
- **Menu screens:** tile sub-lines go to 18 px (overflow fixed), the route-card line to 17 px, the version number to 18 px. `TEXT_MUTED` is lighter, now 4.7 to 5.3:1.
- **16:10:** menus now use the "expand" stretch aspect. The screens stay 1280x720 in the middle and the animated background fills the full 1280x800 screen. The race keeps "keep" with black bars, and nothing changes at 16:9.
- **Full screen:** on first start it defaults to on for screens up to 800 px tall.
- **Tooling:** `SCREEN=1280x800 tools/screenshot.sh` renders on a 1280x800 screen, and screenshots now include the bars. `--input=gamepad|keyboard` sets the input device at startup.

Gamepad-only play was checked by sending real pad events through the running game: title → overwrite-save question → race select → vehicle → start time → stage screen; single stage; leaderboards; options with name entry; pause in the race.

Performance is an estimate, not a measurement on a Deck. `bench_render.gd` on this VM (Xeon 2.1 GHz) gives a median of 5.5 ms for drawing the road by day, 6.1 ms at night and 6.0 ms at night in rain, with p90 peaks up to 11.3 ms. A Deck core (Zen 2 up to 3.5 GHz) should be about as fast, so 60 fps is likely, with rare peaks close to the 16.7 ms frame budget. The GPU load is negligible (2D, 2,500 to 4,300 triangles at 720p).

`docs/steam-deck.md` (German) covers the findings, the changes, a before/after table, remaining limits and recommended settings. It also links the Steam artwork setup in `marketing/steam/README.md`. `docs/ui.md`, `docs/renn-modul.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the README are updated.

The full `tools/run_tests.sh` passes: 242 unit tests (5 new in `test_steam_deck.gd`) and all 9 integration checks.
deviations: Added things the task did not list explicitly, because the controller check turned them up and they were cheap: the on-screen keyboard for the Options name field (NameEntryBox), and tutorial start hints that follow the input device (scripts/race/tutorial_coach.gd, not race_session.gd).

Added a first-start full-screen default on screens up to 800 px tall (Settings.default_fullscreen). Without it the menus would not fill a 16:10 screen, and in desktop mode a 1280x720 window does not fit on the Deck.

Changed the menus to the 'expand' stretch aspect at runtime (GameFlow._set_menu_stretch) and made MenuShell.layer a fixed 1280x720 area in the middle. The project setting stays 'keep', which the race uses.

Changed some colours globally: TEXT_MUTED #626c9c to #7882b2, HUD panel opacity 0.62 to 0.72, speedometer disc 0.70 to 0.78. The HUD refuel and finish overlays moved from y 150 to y 160 because the progress panel is taller.

Screenshots and contact sheets are not in the repo; they are in the scratchpad. The confirm-box and options-keyboard shots, and the gamepad navigation checks, came from small driver scripts in the scratchpad rather than tools/screenshot.sh.
notes_for_lead: The relayed user request ('Steam-Grid-Assets bitte auch im Repository') was already met on main by e38dee9 and da0fee7 (marketing/steam/ with grid, hero, logo, icon, plus tools/steam/ scripts and the README section). I did not duplicate anything; docs/steam-deck.md links to marketing/steam/README.md for setting up the artwork.

Possible merge overlap with the engine-sound agent: small hunks in scripts/ui/game_flow.gd (two places), docs/ui.md (Stil, Dateien, Bedienung, HUD, Debug sections), and a new 'Steam Deck' section in README.md just before 'Steam-Artwork'. I did not touch scripts/audio, race_session.gd, tools/audio or assets/audio.

Not tested on a real Deck. Under Xvfb there is no window manager, so the full-screen request has no effect: the new default sets Settings.fullscreen=true but the window stays at the requested size. The fullscreen path itself is unchanged Godot code (window_set_mode). The gamescope behaviour, the Steam Input mapping and the performance figures in the doc are estimates and are marked as such.

I did not run tests/race/run_race.gd, because it writes savegame and leaderboard files to the shared user:// directory (~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/Crossing Europe – A Racing Xperience). None of my screenshot or driver runs wrote there; they use sample mode or the standalone race scene.

Reusable scratchpad tools in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/engine_v2/deck/bin/: run_shots.sh (all shots at 1280x800), pad_driver.gd (flows options, race, menus, single and keyboard, driven by gamepad events), sheets.sh (contact sheets), contrast.py and inkrows.py (measurements).

Remaining limits, also listed in docs/steam-deck.md: the race keeps 40 px bars because the road renderer is laid out for 1280x720. The smallest texts are at the 9 px x-height minimum. Glyphs are Xbox-style (on the Deck the triggers are called L2/R2 and Start is the ≡ button). The Steam overlay may not pause the race. A key press on a keyboard switches the hints back to keycaps and pad buttons side by side.

result.summary:
I built the offline engine synthesis for Motorklang v2 (tools/audio/engine_synth.py, Python 3 + numpy only, no scipy) and the bank files for all five cars. Nobody could listen during development, so all quality claims below come from measurements; the demos are ready to listen to.

**How the model works**
- **Pulse source:** for every exhaust event, a small cylinder model computes the gas flow out of the exhaust valve (choked and normal flow, reverse flow on overrun when the cylinder is below exhaust pressure). The exhaust port's pressure follows the flow, which limits both the blowdown peak and the overrun backflow.
- **Firing pattern:** real firing orders and intervals. The V8 has the cross-plane 90/180/180/270° spacing per bank; cylinders that open shortly after a bank-mate get a weaker pulse, and this grows toward idle, which produces the burble.
- **Variation:** cycle-to-cycle scatter (stronger at idle), fixed cylinder imbalance, and fuel returning cylinder by cylinder on the way back to idle.
- **Exhaust system per car:** a 1-D acoustic network solved per frequency (header pipes, turbine, catalysts and particle filters, absorptive mufflers with baffle resistances, separate V8 banks with an H-pipe, tailpipe radiation). Speed of sound follows gas temperature, so overrun sounds slightly different from load.
- **Other layers:** strong pulses steepen into shock fronts at full load, valve and tailpipe flow noise, intake (closed throttle on overrun hisses, turbo compressor damps), valvetrain and injector ticks, diesel knock (pilot plus main injection) ringing in the block. Listener is 6 m behind the car with a weak road reflection.
- **Not baked in:** turbo whistle, as the contract requires.

**Bank files** (assets/audio/engines/<car>.json + .f32, in the contract format)
- 32 kHz, 11–14 rpm points from idle to limiter (step ≤ 1.25), both loads, 8 variants, 128-sample overlap.
- Each cycle starts when cylinder 1's pulse front reaches the listener; the travel time (24–30 ms) is stored per bank.
- Clips: crackle (8 variants), blow-off, shift crack and engine start, only where the car physically has them.
- Gearboxes give 1810–2800/min at 130 km/h in top gear and put vmax well below the limiter.
- Size is 1.8–2.3 MB per car, 9.7 MB in total. Rebuilding gives bit-identical files and takes about a minute.

**Reference player** (tools/audio/engine_preview.py) plays the banks exactly as contract §4 describes, driven by a gearbox and vehicle simulation. It renders a ~28 s demo per car and checks the banks.

**Check results**
- **Orders:** the 2nd order dominates the four-cylinders, the 3rd the six-cylinders, the 4th the V8, with half orders at −9 to −18 dB (strongest on overrun).
- **Clicks:** at the ~600–1180 cycle boundaries per demo, the sample jumps equal those at the other cylinders' pulses (ratio 0.98–1.12), and there is no extra high-frequency energy at the splices (ratio ≤ 1.0, diesel max 1.46).
- **Clipping and DC:** no clipping (demo peaks 0.67–0.86 including clips) and no DC offset.
- **Loudness at full throttle:** GT −12.8, sportwagen −16.0, kompakt −17.3, limousine −18.8, kombi −19.4 (K-weighted).
- **On vs. off load:** overrun is 7–12 dB(A) below full load.
- **Cars differ:** full-load spectra differ by 6.3–11.2 dB between any two cars; order patterns only resemble each other for same-cylinder-count pairs.
- **Tests:** tools/run_tests.sh passes, 237 tests with 0 failures, and the integration checks are OK.

Two known weak spots on overrun: near the point where fuel returns (about 1.2–1.6× idle) the waveforms flip polarity, so neighbouring banks blend poorly and the level can dip briefly while the rpm passes through (worst pair: limousine). One sportwagen overrun pair around 3700–4300/min has the same issue.

The deliverables are tools/audio/engine_synth.py, tools/audio/engine_preview.py, the five bank pairs, the `*.f32` export filter, and section 5 of docs/motorsound.md (model, per-car physics choices, how to regenerate, how to tune, results, deviations).
deviations: Bank rpm values are not round numbers (e.g. 699.964 instead of 700): every period is a whole number of samples so all cut points are exact. `period` equals 120·sample_rate/rpm exactly.

The JSON has extra informational fields the runtime can ignore: banks[].delay_ms (pulse travel time used for the cycle start), banks[].level_db (A-weighted bank level) and a top-level 'synth' block (generator, model 2, ref_rpm, loudness_full_db).

The contract says the full-load bank at mid rpm should peak around −3 dBFS. That holds for kompakt and sportwagen; for kombi, limousine and GT the whole car is lowered by 1.8 / 3.9 / 0.9 dB so that no bank exceeds 0.97 (diesel idle knock spikes and bass-heavy low-rpm limousine banks would otherwise clip). mix.gain compensates the loudness.

mix.gain is computed automatically from measured full-load loudness so the loudest car gets 1.0: GT 1.0, sportwagen 0.80, limousine 0.76, kompakt 0.62, kombi 0.47. mix.off_gain is 1.0 except the sportwagen at 0.708 (−3 dB), because its overrun at 8–9k rpm is physically almost as loud as full load.

Clips and layers only exist where the car physically has them: kombi has no crackle, blowoff or shift clips or layers (diesel, no throttle valve, 'kein Knallen'); limousine has no shift clip (torque-converter automatic); sportwagen has no turbo or blowoff (naturally aspirated).
Size: limousine 2.30 MB and GT 2.21 MB, slightly above the ≈1–2 MB guide (each includes a 1.75 s start clip of about 220 KB). The other cars are 1.77–1.96 MB; 9.7 MB in total.

The cycle start ('Eintreffen des Auslassimpulses von Zylinder 1') is taken as the pulse wavefront: exhaust valve opening plus the shortest acoustic path delay at that bank's gas temperature. Overrun banks therefore start about 1 ms later in real time than load banks.

Known limitation: on overrun around the point where fuel returns (about 1.2–1.6× idle), combustion and suction pulses have opposite polarity, so neighbouring banks blend poorly (zero-lag correlation down to 0.05 for the limousine pair 812/1012 rpm) and the level can dip briefly while the rpm passes through. One sportwagen overrun pair at 3671/4334 rpm reaches only 0.16. All full-load pairs are ≥ 0.84.
notes_for_lead: User request relayed in this run ('ich brauche die Steam-Grid-Assets bitte auch im Repository') was not part of this step. The Steam grid assets already exist in the repository at marketing/steam/ (grid_portrait_600x900.png, grid_landscape_920x430.png, @2x versions, hero, logo, icons, README.md; commits e38dee9 and da0fee7, linked from the README section 'Steam-Artwork'). Please confirm with the user whether they need something beyond that.

For the runtime agent, data layout: banks are sorted by rpm ascending, 'off' before 'on' for each rpm. rpm values are non-round; use the float `period`. Linear interpolation is enough (the reference player uses it).

For the runtime agent, missing pieces: the kombi has no crackle, blowoff or shift entries, so the runtime must treat missing clips and layers as off (as the contract allows). The turbo whistle must be synthesized at runtime (the demo uses only a simple stand-in).

For the runtime agent, clip levels: crackle clips peak at 0.75 before layers.crackle.level; blowoff peaks at 0.5; shift at 0.7 and has no level in `layers` (the demo plays it at 0.6). The start clip ends at the level of the idle overrun bank and is meant to crossfade into it (the demo uses 0.15 s).

For the runtime agent, headroom: full-load banks at high rpm peak up to 0.97 before mix.gain, so a bus limiter or a few dB of headroom is advisable for layers playing on top. The demos stay at 0.67–0.86 because crackles play on overrun and the shift crack falls into the shift's load cut.

To regenerate the banks: python3 tools/audio/engine_synth.py (~1 min, bit-identical output). Use --car X to rebuild one car (mix.gain is re-balanced across all cars) and --info to see rpm points, sizes and gearing checks. Demos and checks: python3 tools/audio/engine_preview.py --out DIR.

The demo's acceleration follows the game's VehicleModel curve but is time-compressed so every car reaches ~92 % of vmax in ~11 s. The in-game run-up will be slower. While braking, the sporty cars (kompakt, sportwagen, GT) downshift below 0.45× redline with throttle blips.
All quality judgements come from measurements and spectrograms, not listening. Worth a human listen before merging: the five demo OGGs and all_cars_demo.ogg (paths in review_files).

result.summary:
Runtime for "Motorklang v2", built against docs/motorsound.md. I never had the real banks, so all checks used my own fixture banks.

1. **Bank loader** (`scripts/audio/engine_bank.gd`, class `EngineBank`): reads <car>.json plus the .f32 data and validates the format. Structural problems are errors (the bank is unusable and the old loops play). Deviations the runtime can live with are warnings. All messages are in German.
2. **Gearbox and rpm** (`scripts/audio/engine_gearbox.gd`, class `EngineGearbox`, pure):
   - Automatic-style shifting from the bank's "gearbox": upshift point between the two upshift_rpm values depending on smoothed throttle, downshift with hysteresis, kick-down skipping gears.
   - Near vmax it shifts into the gear that holds vmax lower, so the top gear carries vmax.
   - Braking is detected as speed falling faster than 15 km/h/s with throttle 0. It downshifts gear by gear, with a throttle blip on sporty cars.
   - A shift is a load cut (or blip) plus a quick exponential rpm change.
   - Launch slips at launch_rpm. At standstill it idles in neutral (gear 0) and revs with inertia up to the limiter.
   - No hunting: minimum gap between shifts, a guard after upshifts, and no shift whose new rpm would trigger the opposite shift. rpm always stays within [idle, limiter].
3. **Mixer and playback** (`scripts/audio/engine_audio.gd`, class `EngineAudio`):
   - `render(out, offset, count)` is the pure mixing core and fills any PackedFloat32Array without the AudioServer.
   - Per sample it mixes the two neighbouring rpm banks × both loads at read step rpm/bank_rpm, with log-rpm weights and an equal-power load blend from smoothed load.
   - At every cycle boundary it crossfades over the bank's overlap and picks a random variant (never the same twice in a row). The output has a NaN/inf guard and a soft limit below 1.
   - Layers: turbo whistle with spool lag (only 45 % boost at standstill), blow-off and Poisson-timed crackles on lift-off, limiter cut pattern with a slight rpm droop, shift crack on loaded upshifts, start clip.
   - Live playback runs through an AudioStreamGenerator on bus SFX (mix_rate = bank rate). The fill-ahead is 70 ms by default but grows on its own at low frame rates or with audio drivers that pull large blocks.
4. **Integration:**
   - `AudioManager.set_vehicle(id)` loads the bank on first use and caches it; the race session calls it in `_build`.
   - `set_engine()` is unchanged. New: `engine_state()`, `preview_engine(id)`, `bank_for(id)`, `engine_perf()`.
   - Pause and scene change fade out (0.12 s) and stop filling. Without a bank the old SfxSynth loops play, and `engine_state()` then comes from a generic gearbox.
   - The vehicle screen plays a ~1.5 s rev blip when the selection changes; a running blip fades out first, so two never overlap.
   - Config keys `audio.engine_db`, `engine_latency_s`, `engine_buffer_s`, `engine_preview`, `engine_bank_dir`, with `_doc` text. Debug option `--engine-bank=<bank.json>` plays one bank for every car.
5. **Tests (31 new):** gearbox with five car-shaped profiles, bank validation (good fixture, 5 broken fixture files, in-memory variants), and the mixer: no NaN, peak ≤ 1, variants, cycle length follows rpm, no clicks at boundaries with deliberately different cycles, continuous over an rpm sweep, load blend, limiter pattern, layers, start, fade, preview, and CPU time per frame. Fixtures are generated by the committed `tests/fixtures/make_engine_fixtures.py`.
6. **Demo tool** `tools/audio/render_engine_demo.gd` renders a scripted drive (start, blips, limiter, full throttle through the gears, lift-off, light throttle, braking with downshifts, idle) to a 16-bit WAV. It also has `--only-cycles` and `--trace`.
7. **Docs:** docs/ui.md Audio section with a new "Motor" subsection, ARCHITECTURE.md §11 and §13.

**Results:**
- `tools/run_tests.sh`: 123 scripts compile, 268 tests pass, 0 fail, all 9 integration checks OK.
- CPU per 533-sample frame (32 kHz, best of 5): 0.44 ms (4 sources + turbo), 0.41 ms (limiter at standstill), 0.28 ms (overrun with crackles). Full demo drive: mean 0.38 ms, median 0.33 ms. Budget was < 1 ms.
- A 2 MB bank loads and validates in 1.4 ms.
- In the cycles-only demo render (1.4 M samples) no sample step exceeds the bank's own steepest step, so cycle boundaries, shifts and load changes add no clicks.
- In-game under Xvfb (race scene with autopilot): gears 1→7, pause fades to silence and stops the player, resume works, `stop_all()` resets the engine, and quick double presses on the vehicle screen hand over cleanly.
- Not tested: playback through a real audio device (the container only has the Dummy driver) and the real banks.
deviations: The committed fixture bank fixture_v4 is 16 kHz with a narrow 2000–3900/min range, not the contract's 32 kHz, to keep the binary at 233 KB. The loader reports this as a warning. A contract-compliant full-range 32 kHz V8 demo bank is generated with `make_engine_fixtures.py --demo DIR` and is not committed (2 MB).

Validation severity: things the runtime tolerates are warnings, not errors: below 32 kHz, fewer than 8 variants (at least 2 are required), rpm points more than 1.25 apart, unknown layers or clips, missing layer fields (defaults are used). Anything that breaks playback or reads (format, ranges, lengths, a missing load at an rpm point, period vs rpm off by more than 2 %, overlap below 8, gearbox order) is an error and the old loops play.

Optional bank fields not in the contract, all with defaults: mix.idle_load (0.2, share of the load bank at idle); gearbox.blip (defaults to on when the bank has a 'shift' clip or a 'crackle' layer); gearbox.rev_up_s / rev_down_s (default by fuel and aspiration). They are documented in docs/ui.md only; I did not edit docs/motorsound.md, to avoid conflicts with the synthesis agent.
`engine_state().gear` is 0 for neutral (standstill and free revving at the countdown).

Blow-off plays only on lift-off, not on upshifts (the throttle stays open in automatics/DCTs). Boost at standstill is limited to 45 % because an unloaded engine builds little boost; the contract's description of the layer doesn't cover this.

`set_engine()` keeps its signature but is ignored while the tree is paused and in the same frame as `stop_all()`. Otherwise a race scene being freed would restart the engine for about 0.35 s; the old loops had the same flaw.

The fill-ahead is not a fixed 60–80 ms. The base is `engine_latency_s` = 0.07 s, raised to at least 1.6 smoothed frame times and 1.25 × the largest block the driver pulled between two fills, capped at 90 % of the 0.25 s buffer. With a fixed 70 ms the Dummy driver (about 93 ms blocks) caused about 40 underruns per second; with the adaptive target there were 5 at the start and none after.
The race session passes `vehicle.type_id` (the resolved id, which falls back to the default car for unknown ids) instead of the raw `setup["vehicle"]`.
The vehicle-screen blip plays only when the selection changes, not when the screen opens, and only for cars that have a bank (no blip with the fallback loops). It plays 2 dB below `engine_db`.

In the rpm-sweep test the dropout floor is RMS 0.003 rather than a higher level. Between two rpm points, two banks of the deliberately inconsistent fixture partly cancel (down to about 0.008); a real gap would be about 0.
notes_for_lead: The user request relayed with this run ("oh und ich brauche die Steam-Grid-Assets bitte auch im Repository") was not part of this runtime step, so I did not touch it. The Steam set is already committed on main under marketing/steam/ (grid_portrait_600x900.png and _1200x1800, grid_landscape_920x430.png and _1840x860, hero, logo, icons; made by tools/steam/compose.py, commit e38dee9). Please check with the user whether that covers it or whether they want something else, such as another location or format.

Merging with the synthesis agent: I added `*.f32 binary` to .gitattributes and `*.f32` to export_presets.cfg `include_filter` (the contract requires both). If they made the same edits, expect trivial conflicts. I did not touch tools/audio/engine_synth.py, assets/audio/engines/ or docs/motorsound.md.

After the real banks are merged, run tools/run_tests.sh. The headless race scenes in check_session.gd will then load the banks, and an invalid bank raises `push_error`, which fails the run — a useful gate. Then render all five cars: `for c in kompakt kombi limousine sportwagen gran_turismo; do godot --headless --path . -s res://tools/audio/render_engine_demo.gd -- --bank=res://assets/audio/engines/$c.json --out=/tmp/engine_$c.wav; done` (`--only-cycles` gives the cycle sound alone).

Level: `audio.engine_db` defaults to -3 dB on top of each bank's mix.gain. With my synthetic banks the engine plus crackle and shift clips sometimes reaches the soft limit (above 0.9). Tune engine_db or the banks' clip levels by ear once the real banks are in.

Constraints the real gearboxes should meet (the loader checks the first two):
- upshift_rpm[1] ≤ limiter_rpm
- downshift_rpm below upshift_rpm
- for the top gear to carry vmax: rpm in the top gear at vmax above downshift_rpm[1] + 200; otherwise the car stays one gear lower at vmax, which still works.

Worth adding to motorsound.md §1 so the synthesis agent can set them: gearbox.blip (true/false), mix.idle_load, gearbox.rev_up_s / rev_down_s. Clips play exactly as stored, without a fade-in, so crackle/shift/start clips should begin near 0. My fixture's shift clip starts abruptly and causes the largest sample steps in the full demo.

Not verified here: playback through a real audio device. The container only has the Dummy driver, which pulls about 93 ms blocks. On a real machine or the Steam Deck, `AudioManager.engine_perf()` returns render time per fill and generator underruns (`skips`). Rendering about 1480 samples per fill took about 1.2 ms, which is about 0.43 ms per 533-sample frame.
A HUD rev counter or gear display could read `AudioManager.engine_state()`. I didn't add one, since UI layout was off limits.
Unrelated: running main.tscn with --screen=vehicle prints "2 ObjectDB instances were leaked at exit" even with no input and no blip created, so it predates this work.
